arg.description:
The runtime descriptor stored inside every ArgBuilder. Consumers (parser,
help generator) read this to understand the arg's shape without touching
generics.

configPath.description: Dotted config path for config resolution (e.g. `'deploy.region'`).

defaultDescription.description:
Human-readable replacement for the default value in help, or `false` to
omit the default annotation.

deprecated.description:
Deprecation marker.

- `undefined` — not deprecated (default)
- `true` — deprecated with no migration message
- `string` — deprecated with a reason/migration message

When a deprecated arg is used, a warning is emitted to stderr.
Help text shows `[deprecated]` or `[deprecated: <reason>]`.

elementSchema.description:
Element schema when `kind === 'keyValue'`.

Describes the value of each entry, so `arg.keyValue(arg.number())` decodes
`A=1` to the number `1`. `undefined` leaves entry values as strings.

envVar.description:
Environment variable name for env resolution.

When set and the CLI value is absent, the resolver reads this env var
and coerces the string to the arg's declared kind.

kind.description: What kind of value this arg accepts.

name.description:
A named positional argument entry in the command schema.

Pairs a user-facing arg name with its ArgSchema descriptor.
The array ordering in CommandSchema.args determines CLI position.

presence.description:
Presence describes whether a positional arg is guaranteed to exist when the
action handler runs:

- `'required'`  — must be supplied; error if missing (default)
- `'optional'`  — may be `undefined` if not supplied
- `'defaulted'` — always present (falls back to default value)

sensitive.description: Whether values from this input must be kept out of user-facing projections.

stdin.description:
Stdin binding set by `.stdin()` (`undefined` when the arg never reads
stdin). See StdinBinding.

variadic.description: Whether this arg consumes all remaining positionals.

argElement.description:
Element schema when `kind === 'keyValue'`.

Describes the value of each entry, so `arg.keyValue(arg.number())` decodes
`A=1` to the number `1`. `undefined` leaves entry values as strings.

kind.description: What kind of value this arg accepts.

presence.description: Entry values are required once their containing key-value argument is present.

choice.description: A selectable option for SelectPromptConfig and MultiselectPromptConfig prompts.

description.description: Optional description shown alongside the choice.

label.description:
Display label shown to the user.

Default: value

value.description: The value returned when this choice is selected.

command.description:
Runtime descriptor produced by CommandBuilder.

Consumers (parser, help generator, CLI dispatcher) read this to
understand the command's shape — flags, args, aliases, subcommands,
and interactive resolver.

commands.description:
Nested subcommand schemas (for help rendering and completion).

Pure data — no execution closures. Populated by `.command()` on
`CommandBuilder`. Empty for leaf commands.

flags.description: Named flag schemas, keyed by flag name.

hidden.description: Whether this command is hidden from help listings.

name.description: The command name (used for dispatch, e.g. `'deploy'`).

commandDocument.description:
A single-command definition document, version 1.

Produced by generateCommandSchema. Same shape as a
CommandDefinitionFragmentV1 plus the `schemaVersion` every standalone
document carries.

aliases.description: Alternative names accepted for this command.

args.description: Positional argument definitions in CLI order.

examples.description: Usage examples attached to the command.

flags.description: Named flag definitions keyed by flag name.

hidden.description: Whether the command is omitted from help listings.

name.description: The command name used for dispatch.

schemaVersion.description:
Version of the definition document format emitted by `generateSchema()`
and `generateCommandSchema()` from `@kjanat/dreamcli/json-schema`.

example.description: A single usage example shown in help text.

description.description: Optional description of what this example does.

flag.description:
The runtime descriptor stored inside every FlagBuilder. Consumers (parser,
help generator, resolution chain) read this to understand the flag's shape
without touching generics.

aliases.description: Short/long aliases (e.g. `[{ name: 'f', hidden: false }]` for `--force`).

configPath.description: Dotted config path for v0.2+ resolution (e.g. `'deploy.region'`).

defaultDescription.description:
Human-readable replacement for the default value in help, or `false` to
omit the default annotation.

deprecated.description:
Deprecation marker.

- `undefined` — not deprecated (default)
- `true` — deprecated with no migration message
- `string` — deprecated with a reason/migration message

When a deprecated flag is used, a warning is emitted to stderr.
Help text shows `[deprecated]` or `[deprecated: <reason>]`.

duplicates.description:
How repeated CLI occurrences of a singleton flag combine.

- `'last'`  — last occurrence wins (matches historic behavior)
- `'first'` — first occurrence wins; later ones parse but are ignored
- `'error'` — a second occurrence is a `ParseError` (`DUPLICATE_FLAG`)

Applies to CLI token occurrences only — env/config/prompt/default
resolution keeps its precedence semantics and never raises duplicates.
Occurrences are counted per *logical* flag: aliases and the negated
spelling all count toward the same flag.

Default: `'last'`

envVar.description: Environment variable name for v0.2+ resolution.

kind.description: What kind of value this flag accepts.

negation.description:
Negation settings when `kind === 'boolean'` and `.negatable()` was
called (`undefined` otherwise). See FlagNegation.

presence.description:
Presence describes whether a flag value is guaranteed to exist when the
action handler runs:

- `'optional'`  — not required; unresolved value follows the kind-specific
  optional fallback (`undefined` for most flags, `[]` for arrays)
- `'required'`  — must be supplied; error if missing
- `'defaulted'` — always present (falls back to default value)

prompt.description: Interactive prompt configuration for v0.3+ resolution.

propagate.description:
Whether this flag propagates to subcommands in nested command trees.

When `true`, the flag is automatically available to all descendant
commands. A child command that defines a flag with the same name
shadows the propagated parent flag.

Default: `false`

sensitive.description: Whether values from this input must be kept out of user-facing projections.

stdin.description:
Stdin binding set by `.stdin()` (`undefined` when the flag never reads
stdin). See StdinBinding.

aliases.description: Short/long aliases (e.g. `[{ name: 'f', hidden: false }]` for `--force`).

configPath.description: Dotted config path for v0.2+ resolution (e.g. `'deploy.region'`).

Deprecation marker.

- `undefined` — not deprecated (default)
- `true` — deprecated with no migration message
- `string` — deprecated with a reason/migration message

When a deprecated flag is used, a warning is emitted to stderr.
Help text shows `[deprecated]` or `[deprecated: <reason>]`.

- `'last'`  — last occurrence wins (matches historic behavior)

- `'error'` — a second occurrence is a `ParseError` (`DUPLICATE_FLAG`)

Applies to CLI token occurrences only — env/config/prompt/default

Occurrences are counted per *logical* flag: aliases and the negated

Default: `'last'`

envVar.description: Environment variable name for v0.2+ resolution.

kind.description: What kind of value this flag accepts.

negation.description:
Negation settings when `kind === 'boolean'` and `.negatable()` was
called (`undefined` otherwise). See FlagNegation.

Presence describes whether a flag value is guaranteed to exist when the
action handler runs:

- `'optional'`  — not required; unresolved value follows the kind-specific
  optional fallback (`undefined` for most flags, `[]` for arrays)
- `'required'`  — must be supplied; error if missing
- `'defaulted'` — always present (falls back to default value)

prompt.description: Interactive prompt configuration for v0.3+ resolution.

propagate.description:
Whether this flag propagates to subcommands in nested command trees.

When `true`, the flag is automatically available to all descendant
commands. A child command that defines a flag with the same name
shadows the propagated parent flag.

Default: `false`

stdin.description:
Stdin binding set by `.stdin()` (`undefined` when the flag never reads
stdin). See StdinBinding.

negation.description:
Negation settings for a boolean flag (set by `.negatable()`).

The negated spelling and the positive form are two spellings of ONE
logical flag: they share duplicate policy, and the last CLI occurrence
wins across both. The negated spelling is presence-only — `--no-foo=x`
is rejected.

alias.description:
Explicit negated spelling without the `--` prefix (e.g. `'no-sandbox'`).
`undefined` synthesizes `no-<flagName>` wherever the flag name is known.

hidden.description: Hide the negated spelling from help, completions, and suggestions.

prompt.description:
Discriminated union of all prompt configurations.

Use the `kind` field to narrow:
```ts
if (config.kind === 'select') {
  config.choices // readonly SelectChoice[] | undefined
}
```

choices.description:
Available choices. When omitted for `enum` flags, the enum values
from the flag schema are used automatically.

kind.description:
The kind of interactive prompt to present.

- `'confirm'`     — yes/no boolean question
- `'input'`       — free-text string input
- `'select'`      — single selection from a list
- `'multiselect'` — multiple selections from a list

max.description:
Maximum number of selections allowed.

Default: `Infinity`

message.description: The question displayed to the user.

min.description:
Minimum number of selections required.

Default: `0`

placeholder.description: Placeholder text shown before user types (informational only).

stdin.description: The normalized stdin axis of a flag or an arg.

consume.description: Whether this input consumes the stream alone.

trim.description: Whether one trailing line terminator is dropped from a single value.

when.description: When this input reads the stdin stream.

title: @kjanat/dreamcli definition schema
description:
Runtime descriptor for the CLI program.

Stores the program name, version, description, and registered command schemas.\
Sealed by createCLISchema and rebuilt by each CLIBuilder step.

commands.description: Schemas of the registered commands, in registration order.

defaultCommand.description:
Schema of the default command dispatched when no subcommand matches.

When set, the CLI root behaves like a hybrid command group: subcommands
dispatch by name as usual, but empty argv or flags-only argv falls
through to this command instead of showing root help.

Set via the .default() builder method
or the `defaultCommand` field of CLIDefinition.

name.description: Program name (used in help text, usage lines, and completion scripts).
